entities.summary: Ponhea Yat, also known as Borom Reachea I, was the last king of the Khmer Empire and the first Khmer king of the post-Angkor period. He ascended to the throne in 1448 and ruled until his death in 1463. During his reign, Ponhea Yat oversaw the construction of several temples, including the magnificent Angkor Wat, which became a symbol of Khmer power and culture. His reign also saw the rise of trade and commerce, as Khmer merchants established connections with neighboring kingdoms and foreign powers. Ponhea Yat's legacy extends beyond his own lifetime, as his successors continued to build upon the foundations he laid, shaping the course of Khmer history for centuries to come. Notably, his reign coincided with the rise of the Ayutthaya Kingdom in Siam (modern-day Thailand) and the Ming Dynasty in China, highlighting the complexities of regional politics during this period. Despite his significant contributions, Ponhea Yat's life and reign remain somewhat shrouded in mystery, reflecting the limited documentation available from this era.
